entries.title: Weather transitions and rain history
entries.summary: Weather changes are evaluated when a turn crosses an integer hour. The clear, cloudy and rainy states use ordered checks rather than a single normalized probability table.
entries.conditions: Code-derived thresholds are conditional checks; later checks are reached only if earlier checks fail.

steps: Update the rain-history balance by adding 1/180 while rain power is positive or subtracting 1/360 otherwise, then clamp the balance between minus one and one.
Clear weather tests a cloud threshold of the larger of 0.02 and 0.12 times one minus the balance.
Cloudy weather first tests clearing: the larger of 0.02 and 0.10 times one plus the balance. Only after failure does it test rain: the larger of 0.02 and 0.30 times one minus the balance.
Rain onset from cloudy weather is disabled while daysAlive is below two and the difficulty ID is at most two.

Rainy weather first tests return to clouds using the larger of 0.01 and 0.25 times one plus the balance. Only after failure does it test direct clearing using the larger of 0.01 and 0.05 times one plus the balance.
If rain continues, intensity is perturbed by a random amount between minus 0.10 and plus 0.10 and clamped. Ending rain can fade over subsequent turns.

entries.title: Temperature labels
entries.summary: The UI maps normalized temperature to seven named bands; values above 0.85 use Blazing hot.

steps: Read thresholds in ascending order; each threshold includes equality.
Use the first matching label rather than rounding to a nearby band.
These labels do not by themselves describe clothing, wetness, shade or warmth-loss modifiers.

entries.title: XP thresholds and level-up rewards
entries.summary: Thresholds grow exponentially and are rounded down to a multiple of five. The progression handler checks rounded current XP, retains excess XP and awards one level per handler pass.

steps: For current level L, multiply 28 by 1.2 raised to L, then round the result down to the nearest multiple of five.
Compare rounded current XP with that threshold. A successful increase subtracts the threshold from rounded XP and preserves the remainder.
Award one skill point. Reaching a level divisible by three also grants one HP allocation point.
At the active level cap, the handler holds XP below the next threshold rather than granting another level.

entries.title: Random initialization and saved areas
entries.summary: The inspected paths combine randomized startup, per-area generation and saved-area reuse. A complete reproducible player-facing world-seed contract has not been established.

steps: Game startup randomizes the random-number generator.
The area manager selects a seed from zero to 25000 and initializes random terrain offsets and a noise increment.
Area generation first checks for a saved Ygrid. A previously saved area follows the loading path rather than being regenerated from a guessed seed.
A coordinate helper reseeds from the area seed plus the first coordinate and twenty-two times the second. Other helpers use a factor of 65536 or an offset of 6578 with different generator owners.
The existence of these helpers does not establish their call coverage, RNG compatibility or deterministic replay across versions. A seed finder requires further call-graph and save-state research.

entries.title: Biased loot quantities and value-budget treasure
entries.summary: Loot quantity ranges do not imply equally likely counts. Treasure generation also uses a value budget and rejection rules, not a fixed table of normalized item weights.
entries.conditions: No global item probabilities have been inferred.

steps: The amount helper builds progressively wider inclusive integer draws, then chooses one of those draws uniformly. Low quantities therefore occur more frequently.
The treasure helper repeatedly samples an item ID from zero through 257, rejecting undefined or nonlootable entries and entries that fail budget, minimum-value, type, size or story conditions.
Accepted items reduce the remaining value budget. Defined-item attempts increment a counter capped at 500; undefined-item draws and the early story-gated rejection are not counted.
Durability and stack size can be randomized after selection. Listed shared bonus checks are additive rather than mutually exclusive weights.

entries.title: Workstations, fire and alchemy modifiers
entries.summary: Personal crafting and workstation recipe menus are distinct from lighting a campfire. Base recipes do not include every skill-dependent reduction.

steps: The station initialization explicitly lists separate recipe menus for alchemy stations, the armor workstation, the farmwork table and the chopping log.
The Chopping Log halves the AP cost of firewood recipes.
At station IDs 53, 131 and 172, Brewer multiplies crafting AP by one minus 0.08 per rank, with a nonnegative floor.
At the same station IDs, each ingredient-consumption check can save one required unit with a threshold of 0.20 per completed three Brewer ranks.
A zero-quantity component is a presence requirement rather than a consumed ingredient. Component ID 10000 instead checks a carried tool's chopping capability.
Lighting a fire uses a separate one-AP attempt, fuel and ignition checks. Once lit, a Campfire offers fourteen cooking recipes; a Survivor's Field Kit instead offers fifteen alchemy recipes.
The fire-linked recipe menu is available only while the station has positive active fire time, and is closed when its fire expires.

entries.title: Budgeted creature treasure and recovered projectiles
entries.summary: Raving Unwanted, Mutated Unwanted use budget-generated treasure rather than a fixed item list. Loot-bearing corpse inventories also receive the being's stored arrow entries.
entries.conditions: The corpse must be generated. Stored arrows are not evidence that every fired arrow is recoverable.

steps: The two creature cases call the treasure generator with category one, a total base-value budget of one, and a minimum item value of 0.1.
The generator's type restrictions, nonlootable exclusions, story gates, durability handling and rejection loop still apply.
After the creature-specific base inventory is built, each stored arrow entry is appended. The hit/recovery process that populated that list is a separate mechanic.
